title: Bloch-sphere rotations in driven double-well for ultracold atoms
authors: Michele Modugno, Marco Fattori, Giulio Pettini
abstract: We show that, by using suitable protocols for a non-interacting condensate in a driven double-well, one can achieve controlled rotations about arbitrary axes in the equatorial plane of the Bloch sphere, composed with fast rotations about the $z$-axis. Specifically, we investigate the dynamics induced by a spatially linear time-periodic potential, by means of numerical simulations. We also provide an explicit two-level model that accurately captures the microscopic evolution of the driven system, with the full time-dependent evolution operator obtained using a Floquet-based approach. The analysis is carried out using as a reference a recently realized experimental platform consisting of arrays of double-well potentials based on Beat-Note Superlattices, to which the proposed control scheme is directly applicable.
summary: The authors demonstrate how controlled, arbitrary rotations of pseudospins can be achieved in an ultracold atomic double-well system using fast, time-periodic external driving. By applying Floquet engineering principles, they show that the system's dynamics can be precisely steered to manipulate the Bloch vector along any desired axis in the equatorial plane. This offers a powerful tool for quantum control applications in atom interferometry.
main_problem: The research aims to achieve full coherent control over pseudospin dynamics (Bloch sphere rotations) in a trapped double-well system using time-periodic driving protocols.
main_result: Controlled rotations about arbitrary axes in the equatorial plane of the Bloch sphere can be demonstrated, complementing previous methods that relied only on static biases.
method: The study employs numerical simulations and analytical derivations based on Floquet theory to model the system's time evolution operator.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a non-interacting Bose-Einstein condensate in a double-well potential realized using Beat-Note Superlattices. The dynamics are modeled by an effective two-level Hamiltonian subjected to a spatially linear, time-periodic driving potential.
key_observables: Bloch sphere rotation vector components (n_x, n_y, n_z) and the renormalized Rabi period (T'_R).

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical platform using a static Hamiltonian, then introduces time-periodic driving. It develops the theoretical framework using Floquet theory to derive the evolution operator, before demonstrating two specific protocols (P1 and P2) that achieve controlled Bloch sphere rotations.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete experimental proposals for engineering quantum gates or manipulating spin states in ultracold atom systems by leveraging time-periodic driving fields, which is highly relevant to quantum simulation and measurement techniques in AMO physics.
